target: Does every nontrivial local half-space perturbation bind below the flat attractive Robin threshold, without an ambient-dimension restriction?
hypotheses: Attractive Robin form on H1(Omega), outward normal condition d_nu u=beta u, beta>0; flat threshold -beta^2.
Positive theorem: nontrivial connected smooth compact perturbation in ambient n=2,3; no graph or connected-boundary restriction.
Absence theorem: compactly supported Lipschitz graph in ambient n>=4 and sufficiently weak positive coupling.
accepted_conclusions: Every stated smooth perturbation in n=2,3 binds for every beta>0.
Every compact Lipschitz graph in n>=4 has spectrum and essential spectrum [-beta^2,infinity) at sufficiently weak positive coupling.
Explicit nonzero C-infinity graph f=h/100 in n=4, beta=1, has spectrum [-1,infinity), resolving the dimension-unrestricted universal question negatively.
At every prescribed positive coupling a sufficiently small nonzero smooth compact graph supplies a counterexample in n>=4.
remaining_scope_limits: No general higher-dimensional nongraph classification, no all-coupling absence theorem, no exclusion of embedded eigenvalues, and no novelty certificate. These are not gaps in the dimension-unrestricted negative answer.
